From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@nebulahealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: security@nebulahealth.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible unusual download activity — confirmation needed

Hi Dylan,

We're seeing a spike in outbound connections from one of our integration endpoints to Redwood around 2027-03-31 22:30 UTC. The initial triage flagged a handful of requests that included long context payloads and a higher-than-usual token count. Our security team wants confirmation that (a) there was no data exfiltration from our account, and (b) no customer PII/PHI was persisted or leaked in logs accessible outside our tenancy.

Can you confirm whether Redwood observed any anomalous egress, unusual S3 downloads, or KMS key access patterns tied to our API keys during that window? If possible, please provide a short attestation and the logs you used for the check. We understand reasonable redaction for internal operational details.

We'd appreciate an initial reply within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Sara Mills\Security & Compliance Lead\Nebula Health

Laura / Karthik — forwarding a customer request. Please treat this as internal-only for now.

Ask: quick check and short attestation for Nebula Health covering 2027-03-31 21:00:00 UTC -> 2027-04-01 02:00:00 UTC. Specifically:
- S3 and object-store access: any large GET requests, presigned-url issuance, or bulk object download events tied to Nebula account id
- IAM/KMS events: any KMS Decrypt/Encrypt calls from non-internal principals, or key rotation during window
- Network egress: direction/volume spikes from model-serving nodes, unusual outbound IPs or transfers >100MB
- Audit logs: any logs recorded to external buckets or third-party endpoints referencing customer payloads
- Runtime cache: confirm no model-caching of raw request payloads beyond KV cache TTLs (standard TTL=5m)

If you find nothing suspicious, craft a customer-friendly attestation (one-paragraph plus bullet evidence) and attach supporting excerpts (sanitized). If you find anything ambiguous, escalate to IR with INC-2027-042.

I'll coordinate the reply to Sara.

-Dylan

Dylan / Karthik — quick findings from infrastructure and infra security checks (summarized):

1) S3/object-store access
- Queried object-access logs for Nebula Health account (acct_id: NBL-4483) for 2027-03-31 20:00->2027-04-01 03:00 UTC. No large GETs (>10MB) detected. Several small PUT and GETs consistent with normal model telemetry.
- No presigned-url issuance detected for external principals during the window.

2) KMS / IAM
- KMS: 12 Encrypt/Decrypt calls during the window, all from service principals in our internal keyring. No Decrypts from unknown principals.
- IAM: No token issuance that matches external IPs or unusual user agents.

3) Network egress / transfer volume
- Netflow aggregate: small burst around 2027-03-31 22:28 UTC from the model pool serving the Nebula model alias; peak transfer ~1.6 MB/s for ~90s, total ~180 MB. This matches a high-token generation request pattern from a single client API key. No sustained bulk transfer.
- Outbound connections were to standard cloud vendor IPs (no unknown external endpoints).

4) Audit logs / persisted payloads
- Audit pipeline shows payloads redacted by default in long-term storage. Short-term request logs (retention: 7d) include truncated snippets used for debugging; no full payloads were written to durable external buckets.

5) Runtime cache / model KV
- KV/prefix cache TTLs were respected. No evidence cached payloads exceeded allowed retention.

Conclusion (initial): no evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized persistence outside Nebula's tenancy. Evidence extracts attached: integrity_scan_summary.csv (summary), audit_log_excerpt.txt (sanitized lines), forensic_checklist.pdf (steps taken).

If you'd like, I can expand the CSV with per-request hashes and timestamps for Nebula's security team. Otherwise, I'd propose we send a short attestation to Sara and offer a joint call if they want additional detail.

-Laura

Attachments: integrity_scan_summary.csv, audit_log_excerpt.txt, forensic_checklist.pdf

Hi Sara — thank you for flagging this and for the patience while we completed our checks. Below is our attestation and a short description of the evidence we reviewed.

Attestation (high-level)
- Redwood Inference performed an incident-focused review for Nebula Health covering 2027-03-31 21:00:00 UTC through 2027-04-01 02:00:00 UTC. Based on the checks below, we found no evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized persistence of customer payloads outside Nebula's tenancy. No external principals were observed decrypting Nebula-managed keys or downloading large object sets during the window.

Summary of checks (evidence used)
- Storage access logs: scanned object-store access events for account NBL-4483; no GETs >10MB and no presigned URL issuance to external principals. (See integrity_scan_summary.csv)
- KMS / IAM audit: verified 12 KMS operations were internal-service initiated; no decrypts by unknown principals. IAM token issuance and session start logs show legitimate internal service tokens tied to known agent IDs.
- Network flows: short-lived burst (~1.6 MB/s for ~90s) detected at 2027-03-31 22:28 UTC from the model-serving pool; attributable to a single high-token client request (per API key metadata). Total egress during window ~180 MB — below thresholds we classify as bulk export.
- Logging & persistence: long-term logs redact raw payloads; short-term debugging logs contain truncated request snippets as configured and were not exported to third-party storage. We attached a sanitized excerpt (audit_log_excerpt.txt) showing redaction markers.
- Runtime cache: KV cache TTLs honored; no evidence of payloads cached beyond configured TTLs.

Attachments provided (sanitized)
- integrity_scan_summary.csv — scan summary with aggregated event counts and sizes
- audit_log_excerpt.txt — sanitized lines demonstrating redaction markers and event IDs used for cross-verification
- forensic_checklist.pdf — checklist of commands and queries executed by our team for reproducibility

Next steps and offers
- If Nebula Security wants a deeper, joint forensic session (including per-request hashes and time-aligned packet captures), we can schedule a call and provide additional artifacts under an NDA or joint investigative agreement.
- We will keep the incident record open as INC-2027-042 for 30 days and notify you immediately if any new information emerges.

If you'd like this summarized into a one-paragraph legal attestation on Redwood letterhead, let me know and we can escalate to our compliance team.

Best,
